arxiv-1609-07650.title: Popularity in the generalized Hospital Residents setting
arxiv-1609-07650.creator: Meghana Nasre and Amit Rawat
arxiv-1609-07650.description: Abstract We consider the problem of computing popular matchings in a bipartite graph G = ( ℛ ∪ ℋ , E ) G=(\mathcal{R}\cup\mathcal{H},E) where ℛ \mathcal{R} and ℋ \mathcal{H} denote a set of residents and a set of hospitals respectively.

arxiv-1803-04556.title: Measuring Conflict in a Multi-Source Environment as a Normal Measure
arxiv-1803-04556.creator: Pan Wei 1 , John E. Ball 1 , Derek T. Anderson 1 , Archit Harsh 1 , and Christopher Archibald 2
arxiv-1803-04556.description: Abstract In a multi-source environment, each source has its own credibility. If there is no external knowledge about credibility then we can use the information provided by the sources to assess their credibility. In this paper, we propose a way to measure conflict in a multi-source environment as a normal measure.

arxiv-1909-11395.title: From diffusion in compartmentalized media to non-Gaussian random walks
arxiv-1909-11395.creator: Jakub Ślęzak, Stanislav Burov
arxiv-1909-11395.description: Abstract ABSTRACT. In this work we establish a link between two different phenomena that were studied in a large and growing number of biological, composite and soft media: the diffusion in compartmentalized environment and the non-Gaussian diffusion that exhibits linear or power-law growth of the mean square displacement joined by the exponential shape of the positional probability density.

arxiv-2204-01766.title: A new type of cyclotron resonance from charge-impurity scattering in the bulk-insulating Bi 2 Se 3 thin films
arxiv-2204-01766.creator: Xingyue Han, Maryam Salehi, Seongshik Oh, Liang Wu
arxiv-2204-01766.description: Abstract This work focuses on the low frequency Drude response of bulk-insulating topological insulator Bi 2 Se 3 films. The frequency and field dependence of the mobility and carrier density are measured simultaneously via time-domain terahertz spectroscopy. These films are grown on buffer layers, capped by Se, and have been exposed in air for months.

arxiv-2306-02171.title: The de Rham period map for punctured elliptic curves and the KZB equation
arxiv-2306-02171.creator: Ben Moore
arxiv-2306-02171.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ben Moore. We demonstrate that the algebraic KZB connection of Levin–Racinet and Luo on a once-punctured elliptic curve represents Kim’s universal unipotent connection, and we observe that the Hodge filtration on the KZB connection has a particularly simple form. This allows us to generalise previous work of Beacom by writing down explicitly the maximal metabelian quotient of Kim’s de Rham period map in terms of elliptic polylogarithms.

arxiv-2310-05870.title: Detecting Multipartite Entanglement Patterns using Single Particle Green’s Functions
arxiv-2310-05870.creator: Rajesh K. Malla, Andreas Weichselbaum, Tzu-Chieh Wei, Robert M. Konik
arxiv-2310-05870.description: Abstract We present a protocol for detecting multipartite entanglement in itinerant many-body electronic systems using single particle Green’s functions. To achieve this, we first establish a connection between the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and single particle Green’s functions by constructing a set of witness operators built out of single electron creation and destruction operators in a doubled system.

arxiv-2407-12451.title: Across Platforms and Languages: Dutch Influencers and Legal Disclosures on Instagram, YouTube and TikTok
arxiv-2407-12451.creator: Haoyang Gui, Thales Bertaglia, Catalina Goanta, Sybe de Vries, Gerasimos Spanakis
arxiv-2407-12451.description: Abstract Content monetization on social media fuels a growing influencer economy. Influencer marketing remains largely undisclosed or inappropriately disclosed on social media. Non-disclosure issues have become a priority for national and supranational authorities worldwide, who are starting to impose increasingly harsher sanctions on them.

arxiv-2409-07208.title: Almost-catalytic Computation
arxiv-2409-07208.creator: Sagar Bisoyi, Krishnamoothy Dinesh, Bhabya Deep Rai, Jayalal Sarma ‡
arxiv-2409-07208.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sagar Bisoyi, Krishnamoothy Dinesh, Bhabya Deep Rai, Jayalal Sarma ‡. arxiv-2412-10266.description: Abstract . Stance detection is crucial for fostering a human-centric Web by analyzing user-generated content to identify biases and harmful narratives that undermine trust. With the development of Large Language Models (LLMs), existing approaches treat stance detection as a classification problem, providing robust methodologies for modeling complex group interactions and advancing capabilities in natural language tasks.

arxiv-2503-01652.title: Positive Polytopes with Few Facets in the Grassmannian
arxiv-2503-01652.creator: Dmitrii Pavlov and Kristian Ranestad
arxiv-2503-01652.description: Abstract In this article we study adjoint hypersurfaces of geometric objects obtained by intersecting simple polytopes with few facets in ℙ 5 \mathbb{P}^{5} with the Grassmannian Gr ⁡ ( 2 , 4 ) \mathrm{Gr}(2,4) . These generalize the positive Grassmannian, which is the intersection of Gr ⁡ ( 2 , 4 ) \mathrm{Gr}(2,4) with the simplex.

arxiv-2504-16329.title: Analyzing stripes in crossing pedestrian flows using temporal matrices and a geometric model
arxiv-2504-16329.creator: Piotr Nyczka, Pratik Mullick
arxiv-2504-16329.description: Abstract Understanding pattern formation in crossing pedestrian flows is essential for analyzing and managing high-density crowd dynamics in urban environments. This study presents two complementary methodological approaches to detect and characterize stripe formations, an emergent structure observed when two pedestrian groups cross at various angles.

arxiv-2508-05611.title: Mind the Gap: From Resolving Theoretical Foundations of Chiral(ity)-Induced Spin Selectivity to Pioneering Implementations in Quantum Sensing
arxiv-2508-05611.creator: Yan Xi Foo, Aisha Kermiche, Farhan T. Chowdhury, Clarice D. Aiello, Luke D. Smith
arxiv-2508-05611.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yan Xi Foo, Aisha Kermiche, Farhan T. Chowdhury, Clarice D. Aiello, Luke D. Smith. The chiral(ity)-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, where electrons passing through a chiral medium acquire significant spin-polarization at ambient temperatures, has been widely observed experimentally, yet its theoretical foundations remain actively debated. Open questions persist regarding whether CISS originates from helical geometry or more general chirality, and whether a unified mechanism can account for phenomena across solid-state and soft-matter systems, mesoscopic films, and single molecules.

arxiv-2509-16193.title: Are Multimodal Foundation Models All That Is Needed for Emofake Detection?
arxiv-2509-16193.creator: \authorblockN Mohd Mujtaba Akhtar \authorrefmark 2 \authorrefmark 3 \authorrefmark 1, Girish \authorrefmark 3 \authorrefmark 4 \authorrefmark 1, Orchid Chetia Phukan \authorrefmark 3 \authorrefmark 1, Swarup Ranjan Behera \authorrefmark 5 Pailla Balakrishna Reddy \authorrefmark 6, Ananda Chandra Nay
arxiv-2509-16193.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate multimodal foundation models (MFMs) for EmoFake detection (EFD) and hypothesize that they will outperform audio foundation models (AFMs). MFMs due to their cross-modal pre-training, learns emotional patterns from multiple modalities, while AFMs rely only on audio.

pmc-10738149.title: HEALTH CONDITIONS, CONTROL BELIEFS, AND ATTITUDINAL BELIEFS OF USING TECHNOLOGY IN LOW-INCOME OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10738149.creator: Eunice Oladepe Ojo, Ladda Thiamwong, Rui Xie, Nichole Lighthall, Joon-Hyuk Park, Victoria Loerzel, Jeffrey Stout
pmc-10738149.description: Integrating assistive technologies into fall prevention interventions could improve health outcomes, but older adults in low-income settings face greater challenges with technology use due to factors such as cost, access, and location. We examined the acceptance of technology in low-income older adults and the factors associated with their acceptance.

pmc-11436653.title: The impact of COVID-19 vaccination rate on traffic recovery
pmc-11436653.creator: Suyanpeng Zhang, Jing Jin, Han Yu, Ying Hong, Neeraj Sood, Sze-chuan Suen
pmc-11436653.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). At the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic in the US, traffic sharply fell due to social distancing policies in many locations. Correspondingly, many regions observed an increase in traffic volume (traffic recovery) as the pandemic eased in 2022. We examine how vaccination rates influence traffic recovery in Los Angeles County (LAC), controlling for differences in case counts, demographics, and socioeconomic factors across areas with different vaccination rates.

pmc-11454561.title: 8050 Incidence And Geographic Distribution Of Pheochromocytoma And Paraganglioma In The Slovak Population
pmc-11454561.creator: I Jochmanova, M Ircha
pmc-11454561.description: Disclosure: I. Jochmanova: None. M. Ircha: None.Pheochromocytoma (PHEO) and Paraganglioma (PGL) are neuroendocrine tumors originating from chromaffin tissues of the adrenal medulla or extra-adrenal paraganglia and are characterized by catecholamine overproduction. Excess of catecholamines and the risk of metastatic disease lead to increased morbidity and mortality as well as decreased quality of life of patients.

pmc-11486892.title: Copper-Based Nanomedicines for Cuproptosis-Mediated Effective Cancer Treatment
pmc-11486892.creator: Dahye Noh, Hokyung Lee, Sangmin Lee, In-Cheol Sun, Hong Yeol Yoon
pmc-11486892.description: The recent discovery of cuproptosis, a novel copper-ion-induced cell death pathway, has suggested the novel therapeutic potential for treating heterogeneous and drug-resistant cancers. Currently, copper ionophore-based therapeutics have been designed to treat cancers, utilizing copper ions as a strategic tool to impede tumor proliferation and promote cellular demise.

pmc-11690170.title: EFFECTS OF POSTRETIREMENT ACTIVITIES ON RETIREES’ WELL-BEING: THE MODERATING ROLE OF CHILDLESSNESS
pmc-11690170.creator: Gloria Lin, Edwin Ka Hung Chung, Dannii Y Yeung, Alvin Ho, Amy Ng
pmc-11690170.description: According to role theory, retirees’ work roles are likely diminished upon retirement, but their family and community roles are strengthened. Such pattern however may be different among childless retirees as their family roles are comparatively fewer than retirees with children.

pmc-13411937.title: Multi-class, unsupervised detection and classification of biological and anthropogenic sounds in coral reefs
pmc-13411937.creator: Daniel Duane, Matthew T. Duggan, Erika Berlik, Marc S. Dantzker, Aaron N. Rice, Lauren A. Freeman
pmc-13411937.description: Analyzing the complex and diverse soundscapes of ecosystems such as coral reefs remains a challenge for understanding environmental dynamics and processes. While machine learning techniques can significantly improve detection and classification capabilities, applications of traditional supervised learning to underwater acoustics are limited by the size and class-coverage of labeled datasets.

pmc-13569205.title: Abundance of atrazine degrading genes trzN versus atzA in soil cultures and in situ degradation rates
pmc-13569205.creator: Truphena Akinyi, Damiana Diaz‐Reck, Aman Raj, Anat Bernstein
pmc-13569205.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BACKGROUNDAtrazine is a widely used herbicide whose persistence and mobility have led to frequent contamination of soils and water bodies. Atrazine can be degraded in soils through two primary biotic pathways: an oxidative route that produces the relatively persistent metabolites desethylatrazine and deisopropylatrazine, and a hydrolytic route mediated by chlorohydrolases encoded by atzA or trzN, leading to the less recalcitrant intermediate hydroxyatrazine.

pmc-13674893.title: Autologous blood-assisted closure of an unanticipated posterior scleral perforation: A novel rescue technique
pmc-13674893.creator: Günhal Şatırtav, Hürkan Kerimoğlu, Mehmet Adam
pmc-13674893.description: The surgical challenge of intraocular foreign bodies (IOFBs) in the posterior pole is compounded by the fact that posterior scleral perforations are often not anticipated preoperatively. We describe a novel, simplified rescue technique using an autologous blood clot to seal a traumatic posterior scleral defect.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Amount There are authorized to be appropriated to the Fund $50,000,000 to carry out this subchapter. uslaw-usc-t49-s31132.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s31132.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part B (Commercial); Chapter 311 (Commercial Motor Vehicle Safety); Subchapter III (Safety Regulation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this subchapter— (1) “commercial motor vehicle” means a self-propelled or towed vehicle used on the highways in interstate commerce to transport passengers or property, if the vehicle— (A) has a gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle.
